source.text:
This may just be cope, but I still see this playing out as a strong negative for the low-end developers and a neutral or positive for seniors.

So much of what I do every day are non-coding jobs that aren't actually that easy to do with AI (of course that's not technically true but as a practical matter corporate America is probably not going to change all that fast, we've had lots of automation abilities for years that they still don't embrace with any great amount of success).

But what about the team of Genpact developers I have in Hyderbad & Bengalaru? They're coders, and I know already that I can take what I give them and run it through Claude Code myself and get results 100x faster, with better quality to boot. With less of my time needed to review & provide feedback. These guys, love 'em, but they're fucked. I've been trying to help them level up, but they're mostly freshers and it is a steep climb.

Luckily our senior management is still slow-walking our foray into LLM coding, but I know my manager already sees the writing on the wall (though he's more worried about his own job than ours).
